title: Quality vs Quantization (FP8/INT8) — Evals Summary (Hosted Catalog) — Sprint Readout v1
content:
Context / why this doc exists
- This is the Applied ML + Evals summary of quality deltas observed when enabling quantized kernel paths (FP8 + INT8 variants) vs baseline (BF16/FP16) on the Top Hosted Models Benchmark Suite v3.
- Goal: enable kernel/scheduler perf wins without shipping silent quality regressions. This doc feeds:
  - Quantization default policy (which modes can be default by model/SKU)
  - Canary gating criteria (quality + user-visible metrics)
  - Customer comms / what we can claim (internal + external)

Scope
- Models evaluated (hosted catalog “top traffic” subset for sprint; names are internal catalog aliases):
  1) Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct ("ll3-70b")
  2) Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct ("ll3-8b")
  3) Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct ("mix-8x7b")
  4) Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct ("qwen-72b")
  5) Mistral-7B-Instruct ("mis-7b")
  6) (limited) Tool-calling tuned variant used by a subset of hosted traffic ("toolchat-mid")

- Quantization modes tested
  - Baseline: BF16/FP16 (as configured in current hosted runtime)
  - FP8 kernels: FP8 attention + FP8 matmul paths where available (runtime flag-gated)
  - INT8 kernels: INT8 matmul path (shape-guarded + fallback)

- GPUs (quality runs only)
  - H100: primary
  - A100: spot-check only (we do not expect quality differences from GPU, but included to catch nondeterminism / kernel-path divergence).

Methodology (how to interpret numbers)
- Prompt sets: Benchmark Suite v3 (production-like distributions)
  - Summarization + synthesis (short + long)
  - RAG-style answers (with citations-like format constraints)
  - Code generation + bugfix
  - Tool calling + structured output (JSON schema / function args)
  - Long-context QA (8k–32k contexts; sampled)

- Metrics we report (per model, by task slice)
  1) Preference win-rate vs baseline (pairwise judge; same sampling seed where possible)
  2) Structured output validity rate (JSON parse + schema checks)
  3) Task-specific scores (lightweight):
     - Summarization: ROUGE-L (proxy only; we weight preference higher)
     - Code: unit-test pass rate on a small curated set
     - RAG QA: exact match / citation format validity proxy

- Sampling / determinism
  - Temperature and top_p pinned per suite defaults.
  - 3 independent runs for the “quality sanity suite” (PR-519) and 1 run for the full v3 suite (time-bound).
  - We treat small deltas (< ~1–2% absolute on preference win-rate) as noise unless concentrated in a slice or correlated with user-facing incidents.

- Decision thresholds (proposed for defaults)
  - Block default enablement if:
    - Overall preference win-rate drops by >= 3% absolute AND confirmed in rerun
    - Any structured-output validity drop >= 0.5% absolute on tool/JSON slices (because even small drops can cause hard failures)
    - Long-context slice shows consistent judge preference drop >= 5% absolute (these regressions show up as “subtle wrongness”)
  - Allow default enablement with guardrails if:
    - Overall preference within ±2% and no hard-failure slices regress
    - Any regressions are isolated + we can gate by context length / task type / shape regime


Executive summary (what we found)
- FP8
  - Net: generally neutral-to-positive on short/medium context for most models; biggest risk is long-context correctness/faithfulness degradation on specific architectures.
  - Most notable issue this sprint: ll3-70b shows a repeatable quality regression on long-context QA and multi-doc synthesis when FP8 attention is enabled for long prefill + long decode.
  - Tool/JSON validity: no meaningful FP8-specific drop observed overall, but we saw a small increase in “near-miss JSON” (extra trailing commas) on toolchat-mid under one prompt cluster; did not reproduce in rerun.

- INT8
  - Net: mostly neutral on code + generic chat; slightly worse on summarization + “tone/nuance” tasks for two model families, but within our default thresholds in most slices.
  - The major risk is calibration / activation distribution sensitivity: summarization workloads with long-ish outputs (512–1024 tokens) showed a preference drop on qwen-72b and mix-8x7b.
  - Tool/JSON validity: INT8 is OK on validity rate in our suite; however, we have one customer-facing concern (SUP-31852) that maps to summarization-style prompts (not structured outputs). Recommend we do not position INT8 as “always safe” for summarization without opt-in or eval sign-off.

- Recommendation for hosted defaults (proposed)
  - ll3-8b, mis-7b: FP8 default OK (subject to long-context gating), INT8 default OK for cost-focused SKUs.
  - mix-8x7b: FP8 default OK for <= 8k context; INT8 default not recommended for summarization-heavy tenants without eval sign-off.
  - qwen-72b: FP8 default OK for <= 8k context; INT8 default should remain opt-in pending calibration refinement.
  - ll3-70b: FP8 should NOT be default for long-context; allow FP8 for short/medium contexts with a strict guard (context length + prefill regime) and canary monitoring; INT8 is acceptable but watch summarization nuance.


Detailed results (high level)
Note: numbers are “directional” for sprint decisions; not approved for external sharing. All deltas are vs baseline.

1) Overall preference win-rate vs baseline (aggregate across suite)
- ll3-70b:
  - FP8: -2% overall (but -7% to -10% on long-context slice; see below)
  - INT8: -1% overall (within noise)
- ll3-8b:
  - FP8: +1% overall (noise / judge variance)
  - INT8: ~0% overall
- mix-8x7b:
  - FP8: +0% overall
  - INT8: -2% overall, concentrated in summarization
- qwen-72b:
  - FP8: -1% overall
  - INT8: -3% overall (borderline), concentrated in summarization + synthesis
- mis-7b:
  - FP8: +1% overall
  - INT8: -1% overall
- toolchat-mid:
  - FP8: ~0% overall
  - INT8: ~0% overall

2) Structured output / tool calling validity
- Metric: valid JSON + schema-conformant args (% of tool prompts)
- Baseline validity across models: 98.6%–99.4% depending on model
- Observed deltas:
  - FP8: within ±0.1% for all models (no persistent drop)
  - INT8: within ±0.2% for all models (no persistent drop)
- One-off observation: toolchat-mid FP8 run showed a +0.3% increase in “JSON trailing token noise” (still parseable; not counted as invalid). Did not reproduce.

3) Task-slice notes (where regressions cluster)
A) Long-context QA / synthesis (8k–32k)
- ll3-70b + FP8: consistent regression.
  - Symptoms:
    - More "hallucinated bridging" between distant context segments
    - Slightly worse citation anchoring in our proxy format checks
    - Higher judge preference for baseline due to factuality/faithfulness
  - Hypothesis (not fully proven): FP8 attention path sensitivity to very long sequence + KV/cache alignment edge cases (runtime also has a related fix PR-19871). Even after alignment fix, the quality regression persists in our rerun, though the magnitude is smaller.
  - Mitigation recommendation:
    - Gate FP8 attention for ll3-70b when (context_len > 8k) OR (prefill_tokens > threshold) until we have a targeted fix + rerun.
    - Keep FP8 matmul allowed if the attention path is baseline (if runtime supports mixed selection).

- qwen-72b + FP8: mild regression (-3% to -4% on long-context), not a hard stop but suggests similar sensitivity. Recommend same gating (<= 8k default) until we expand coverage.

B) Summarization (short input, long output)
- INT8 regressions show up here more than elsewhere.
  - mix-8x7b + INT8: -4% to -6% preference on summarization slice (mostly “loss of nuance” + more repetition at the end of long generations).
  - qwen-72b + INT8: -5% to -8% preference on summarization + synthesis; ROUGE-L not dramatically worse, but judges prefer baseline.
  - ll3-* + INT8: largely neutral.
- Mitigation recommendation:
  - Keep INT8 opt-in for mix-8x7b and qwen-72b until we do:
    1) improved calibration set specifically including summarization-style activations and longer outputs
    2) per-task routing option in Optimize guidance (or at least doc disclaimers)
  - For hosted defaults: allow INT8 for these models only on cost-focused SKUs behind a “quality-sensitive workload” warning, and strongly recommend customer eval if summarization is primary.

C) Code + tool calling
- No meaningful regressions found for FP8/INT8 in our code slice (unit-test pass rate within noise across runs).
- Tool calling validity stable as noted above.
- Practical note: even when validity rate is stable, some FP8/INT8 outputs include slightly more whitespace / formatting drift. For most tool runtimes this is irrelevant, but worth monitoring in strict JSON parsers.


Model-by-model recommendation (policy draft)
Legend:
- OK-default: can enable by default (subject to standard perf canary)
- OK-guarded: enable by default only with explicit gating rules
- Opt-in: available but not default; require eval sign-off for certain workloads

- ll3-70b
  - FP8: OK-guarded
    - Default for <= 8k contexts; disable for > 8k until rerun shows no regression.
    - Add an internal note: “If customer is long-context heavy, keep baseline attention.”
  - INT8: OK-default (with monitoring)

- ll3-8b
  - FP8: OK-default
  - INT8: OK-default

- mix-8x7b
  - FP8: OK-default (<= 8k contexts)
  - INT8: Opt-in (summarization risk)

- qwen-72b
  - FP8: OK-guarded (<= 8k contexts)
  - INT8: Opt-in (summarization + synthesis risk)

- mis-7b
  - FP8: OK-default
  - INT8: OK-default

- toolchat-mid
  - FP8: OK-default
  - INT8: OK-default


Operational guidance (what to do in rollout/canary)
- Canary quality signals to monitor (in addition to latency/TTFT/TPOT)
  - Tool/JSON invalid rate (hard failures) by model + kernel mode
  - "Answer correctness" proxies we already collect for some cohorts:
    - user thumbs-down rate
    - automatic "retry" rate (client retry / regeneration)
    - short-term session abandonment (proxy)
  - Long-context cohorts: isolate by request context length bucket if possible.

- Rollback triggers (quality)
  - If JSON invalid rate increases by >= 0.3% absolute sustained over 30 minutes for a canary cohort: rollback immediately.
  - If customer support reports “silent wrong answers” correlated with FP8 enablement for ll3-70b long-context: rollback FP8 for >8k globally (we have a strong prior here).

- Customer-facing posture (internal note)
  - We can say: “Quantized kernels typically preserve output quality; in rare cases quality may vary by model and workload; we provide controls + canary rollouts.”
  - We should NOT claim: “No quality impact” or “bitwise identical outputs.”


Open questions / follow-ups
1) ll3-70b FP8 long-context regression root cause
- Action: run targeted long-context eval with additional seeds and collect Nsight traces for the worst cases (coordinate with runtime team thread asking for traces).
- Owners: Priyanka (eval reruns), Rina (harness), Hiro/Grace (kernel investigation partner).

2) INT8 summarization sensitivity
- Action: build a summarization-heavy calibration set + re-quantize qwen-72b and mix-8x7b; rerun summarization slice.
- Owners: Arjun + Olivia.

3) Standardize gating knobs
- We need a consistent “context_len threshold” definition across evals vs runtime flags vs console metrics.
- Owner: Claire to propose a single definition and ensure dashboards align.


Appendix A — Run notes / caveats
- Judge variance: some slices are inherently noisy. The long-context ll3-70b FP8 regression is NOT noise; it reproduced.
- We intentionally did not chase tiny deltas (<1%) unless correlated with a real incident or a consistent slice-specific pattern.
- These results reflect runtime state during the sprint; kernel fixes (e.g., KV cache alignment) can shift outcomes. Re-run is required before making an external benchmark claim.

Appendix B — Quick table (policy snapshot)
Model | FP8 default | INT8 default | Notes
- ll3-70b | GUARDED | YES | FP8 long-context regression; gate >8k
- ll3-8b | YES | YES | No material regressions
- mix-8x7b | YES (<=8k) | OPT-IN | INT8 summarization preference drop
- qwen-72b | GUARDED (<=8k) | OPT-IN | INT8 summarization/synthesis drop; FP8 mild long-context sensitivity
- mis-7b | YES | YES | Stable
- toolchat-mid | YES | YES | Stable; monitor JSON near-miss noise

Changelog
- 2026-02-27 (Jonas): incorporated rerun confirming ll3-70b FP8 long-context regression; updated policy table; added rollout triggers.
- 2026-02-22 (Olivia): added summarization slice notes mapping to SUP-31852.
- 2026-02-18 (Arjun): initial INT8 results + calibration caveats.
